newsitem.title: GERMANY: Peacekeepers should stay on in Bosnia - U.N. general.
newsitem.headline: Peacekeepers should stay on in Bosnia - U.N. general.

text.p: The head of U.N. peacekeepers said on Friday a NATO-led force of at least 20,000 troops should stay on in former Yugoslavia once the current 12-month mandate runs out in December.

Lieutenant-General Manfred Eisele said that when the present peacekeeping force (IFOR) withdraws it should leave behind a smaller and very flexible contingent of "firemen" until military equilibrium between former foes in the region has been established.
"We must at least leave a contingent of firemen behind," Eisele, who is German, said in a speech addressed to the Society for Foreign Policy in Berlin.
He said it was now generally agreed that the expiry of IFOR's mandate should not necessarily mean complete withdrawal from the once war-torn region.
"A continued military presence is necessary," said Eisele, who is the top military advisor to U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali.
About 50,000 troops from 34 countries under American leadership are deployed in Bosnia to help implement the Dayton peace accord which ended 43 months of war last December.

NATO-led IFOR's mandate runs out in December, but plans are already under way to begin pulling out after Bosnian elections. It is still not certain whether some form of security force will remain after the official IFOR pull-out.
German leaders have been outspoken on the subject while most NATO members have kept quiet and Washington has refused to comment until after U.S. elections on November 5.

Germany's Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Defence Minister Volker Ruehe have both said some kind of security force was needed there until military equilibrium between the former warring parties had been established. They said that the force would probably include German troops.
